blogs.title: When Threats Aren’t Persecution: The Tenth Circuit’s Narrow View of Past Harm in Asylum Cases
blogs.description: This post dissects the Court’s reliance on precedent that threats and psychological distress alone do not satisfy the ‘past persecution’ prong. It will evaluate the cumulative‑effects doctrine, compare Jimenez v. Bondi to other circuits that have recognized broader harms, and consider the policy implications for asylum seekers facing organized‑crime violence in weak‑state contexts.

blogs.title: Political Opinion or Personal Grievance? Navigating the Nexus Requirement After Jimenez
blogs.description: An analysis of the Court’s application of the ‘central reason’ test for nexus, focusing on how the decision distinguishes political motivation from personal vendettas tied to criminal enterprises. The article will explore divergent circuit approaches to mixed‑motive persecution and anticipate how future litigants might better frame political opinion claims against narco‑political actors.

blogs.title: The ‘Unable or Unwilling’ Standard and Internal Relocation: Lessons from the Colombian Context
blogs.description: A close look at the Court’s treatment of government‑protection arguments, emphasizing the evidentiary burden on asylum seekers to show systemic state failure. The post will assess the court’s deference to police testimony, the role of reporting requirements, and the broader trend of courts demanding concrete proof of state incapacity, especially in countries with entrenched criminal‑government overlap.

blogs.title: Safe Relocation Myths: How the Tenth Circuit Interprets Internal Relocation Feasibility
blogs.description: This entry examines the Court’s brief discussion of internal relocation, analyzing why the brief three‑week stay in the Bogota countryside was deemed sufficient. It will contrast the decision with other appellate rulings that require more rigorous proof of risk, and discuss the practical hurdles asylum seekers face when courts expect relocation as a viable safety net.
